split_reasoning: One activity: writing up each customer contact or transaction; inquiries, complaints, and comments are just different contents of the same record.

parts.text: Record the details of a customer interaction or transaction, including the inquiry, complaint, or comment and the actions taken.
parts.type_reasoning: Each write-up is a distinct account note that colleagues and later reps rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Reps write one note per contact in the CRM or account system; this is the step's own output, separate from handling the contact itself.
parts.work_item: one interaction record written after a customer contact
parts.start: customer contact or transaction ends (or wrap-up time begins)
parts.end: note with reason for contact, details, and actions taken saved to the customer's account
parts.checked_by: other reps who handle the account later; quality-assurance reviewer or supervisor

split_reasoning: Exchanging merchandise, refunding money, and adjusting bills are alternative remedies for the same deliverable, a resolved complaint, so no split.

parts.text: Resolve a customer's service or billing complaint by processing an exchange, refund, or bill adjustment.
parts.type_reasoning: Each complaint ends in a processed remedy that the customer and billing/finance rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Complaints are handled and closed one case at a time, with the remedy transaction as the handed-over output.
parts.work_item: one complaint resolved with an exchange, refund, or bill adjustment processed
parts.start: complaint accepted as valid and remedy chosen
parts.end: exchange, refund, or adjustment entered in the system and case marked resolved
parts.checked_by: customer; billing or finance team; supervisor who approves adjustments above limits

notes: Boundary with 2585 (assessing complaint validity) and 18565 (taking complaint details) is a judgment; this part covers only the remedy step.

split_reasoning: One activity: verifying that a promised fix actually took effect.

parts.text: Check that the changes made to resolve a customer's problem (e.g. an adjustment, order, or account change) were actually carried out.
parts.type_reasoning: Each check produces a confirmed (or reopened) case that the customer and team rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Follow-up checks are done per case, typically from a follow-up queue or callback reminder.
parts.work_item: one resolved case verified (follow-up check on a customer's fix)
parts.start: follow-up reminder or case due for verification
parts.end: change confirmed in the account/order system and case closed, or discrepancy flagged and case reopened

split_reasoning: Responding to inquiries and notifying customers of claim results or adjustments are both outbound customer contacts that deliver an answer or outcome, so they are treated as one activity.

parts.text: Contact a customer (by phone, email, or letter) to answer a pending inquiry or to tell them the outcome of a claim investigation or a planned adjustment.
parts.type_reasoning: Each contact delivers a specific answer or decision the customer relies on, whether by call or written notice.
parts.unit_reasoning: Outbound contacts are worked one case at a time from a callback or notification queue.
parts.work_item: one outbound customer response or notification sent/completed
parts.start: case reaches a decision or pending inquiry is ready for reply
parts.end: customer reached (or written notice sent) with the answer, outcome, or planned adjustment, and contact logged

notes: Could be split into 'answer pending inquiries' vs 'notify claim outcomes'; also could be LIVE_SERVICE when done by phone. The inquiry-answering portion is close to 18565.

split_reasoning: One activity: escalating an unresolved grievance to another department.

parts.text: Refer an unresolved customer grievance to the designated department for further investigation.
parts.type_reasoning: Each referral is a hand-off package the receiving department relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Referrals are made as one escalation ticket or transfer per grievance; this is the step's own output.
parts.work_item: one escalation/referral of an unresolved grievance
parts.start: rep determines the grievance cannot be resolved at their level
parts.end: escalation ticket with case summary routed to the designated department and customer informed
parts.checked_by: receiving department (e.g. claims, billing, investigations); supervisor

split_reasoning: Determining charges, collecting a deposit or payment, and arranging billing are successive steps in settling one service request's money side, so no split.

parts.text: Determine the charges for a customer's requested service and collect the deposit or payment or set up billing for it.
parts.type_reasoning: Each request ends in a priced, paid-or-billed transaction that finance relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Charges and payments are entered per service request or account transaction.
parts.work_item: one service request priced and payment collected or billing arranged
parts.end: charges calculated and quoted, and payment/deposit posted or billing set up on the account
parts.checked_by: customer; billing/finance team; cash reconciliation or audit

notes: Usually done during a live call (18565); in-person payment collection may involve some cash handling.

split_reasoning: Contract forms, change-of-address records, and discontinuance orders are different document types but the same kind of work: processing an account change on the computer, so no split.

parts.text: Complete a contract form, change-of-address record, or service discontinuance order in the computer system.
parts.type_reasoning: Each form or order is a distinct record that downstream teams act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Each account change is entered and submitted as one form or order.
parts.work_item: one account form or service order completed (contract, address change, or discontinuance)
parts.start: customer request with needed details received
parts.end: form or order completed and submitted in the system

notes: Partly overlaps 18565, which mentions taking orders and cancelling accounts during the conversation; this statement covers the back-end paperwork.

split_reasoning: One activity: investigating a complaint to judge its validity and likely cause; the listed information sources are inputs.

parts.text: Gather and examine the relevant information on a customer complaint to decide whether it is valid and what likely caused it.
parts.type_reasoning: Each investigation ends in a validity finding that the resolution step relies on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Complaints are investigated one case at a time, ending in a recorded determination.
parts.work_item: one complaint investigated with validity and probable cause recorded
parts.end: determination (valid/not valid, probable cause) recorded on the case
parts.checked_by: supervisor; billing or claims department; customer via the eventual decision

split_reasoning: One activity: pitching new or additional products or services to customers.

parts.text: Solicit sales of new or additional services or products from customers.
parts.type_reasoning: The value is in persuading the customer during the live contact; any resulting order is entered under another statement.

notes: Could alternatively be LIVE_SERVICE with 'one sales offer made / order taken' as the item; the order entry itself overlaps 18565.

split_reasoning: One activity: making a coverage determination for a reported loss.

parts.text: Review the terms of a customer's insurance policy to determine whether a reported loss is covered.
parts.type_reasoning: Each review produces a coverage decision that the customer and claims staff rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Coverage is checked per reported loss or claim inquiry.
parts.work_item: one coverage determination for a reported loss
parts.start: customer reports a loss or asks whether it is covered
parts.end: coverage decision (covered / not covered / refer) recorded and communicated

split_reasoning: Two activities: physically comparing returned merchandise against the requisition and invoice, and then preparing an invoice for the returned goods at a computer.

parts.text: Inspect disputed or returned merchandise and compare it with the original requisition and invoice details.
parts.type_reasoning: Requires handling and examining the physical goods away from a computer.

parts.text: Prepare an invoice (credit or return invoice) for returned goods.
parts.type_reasoning: Each return produces an invoice that billing and the customer rely on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Return invoices are prepared one per return or dispute.
parts.work_item: one return invoice prepared for a disputed shipment
parts.start: comparison of returned goods against requisition and invoice completed
parts.end: return/credit invoice issued and posted to the account

notes: Whether the comparison is hands-on depends on the setting; if done from documents only, part a would be DISCRETE and merge with b.

split_reasoning: One activity: proposing changes to prevent recurring problems; products, packaging, shipping, service, and billing are just subject areas.

parts.text: Recommend improvements to products, packaging, shipping, service, or billing procedures to prevent future customer problems.
parts.type_reasoning: Each recommendation is a written suggestion that management reviews and may act on.
parts.unit_reasoning: Reps hand over recommendations as individual suggestions or feedback submissions, often based on recurring complaints.
parts.start: rep notices a recurring problem pattern
parts.end: written suggestion or feedback submitted to supervisor or the responsible department
parts.checked_by: supervisor or management of the responsible department

notes: Some recommendations may be given verbally in team meetings, which would be INTERPERSONAL.

split_reasoning: Providing information, taking orders, cancelling accounts, and taking complaint details are different request types handled within the same live customer contact, so no split.

parts.text: Handle a customer's phone or in-person contact: provide product or service information, take or enter an order, cancel an account, or take details of a complaint.
parts.type_reasoning: A live conversation with a customer that ends in a resolved request or a record of it.
parts.unit_reasoning: The call or walk-up contact is the unit that enters the queue and is closed.
parts.work_item: one customer call or walk-up contact handled
parts.start: customer's call is answered or customer approaches the counter
parts.end: information given, order entered, account cancelled, or complaint details captured, and contact ends
parts.checked_by: customer; quality-assurance call monitoring or supervisor

notes: Record-keeping after the contact is 2578; back-end form completion is 2584.
